sections.Highlights: THIS... is a 2011 BMW 1M, finished in Black Sapphire Metallic with a black interior. Cars & Bids managing editor Kennan Rolsen reviewed this 1M, and the video is viewable below. This 1M is equipped with a 6-speed manual transmission, and its odometer currently displays about 2,900 miles. The attached Carfax history report contains some gaps, though it shows no accidents or mileage discrepancies in this BMW's past; it also lists registrations in California from new. According to the window sticker provided in the gallery, factory equipment includes the Navigation Assist, Premium 2, and Convenience packages, 19-inch Style 359M wheels, a variable M differential lock, an M-specific suspension system, xenon headlights, Boston leather upholstery, heated front sport seats, a Harman/Kardon sound system, and more as listed below. The only modification reported by the selling dealer is a set of black kidney grilles. The M version of BMW's 1 Series coupe, called E82 internally, was intended to be a limited-production model but it proved popular enough to warrant tripling the original production quota to just over 6,300 units. Its turbocharged engine was a polarizing departure from previous M cars, as was its funky styling — and yet, the 1M has gained a substantial and loyal following since production ended in 2012. Power comes from a 3.0-liter twin-turbocharged straight-6, rated at 335 horsepower and 332 lb-ft of torque. Called N54T internally, it spins the rear wheels via a 6-speed manual transmission.
